quote: Human beings have rights, because they are moral beings: the rights of all men grow out of their moral nature; and as all men have the same moral nature, they have essentially the same rights.
source: Angelina Grimké, Letters to Catherine E. Beecher, Letter XII, Human Rights Not Founded on Sex, 2 October 1837 (Isaac Knapp, 1838)

evidence.where: the full text of the 1838 Isaac Knapp edition, read line by line
evidence.edition: Letters to Catherine E. Beecher, Boston, printed by Isaac Knapp, 25 Cornhill, 1838
evidence.locator: Letter XII, Human Rights Not Founded on Sex, headed East Boylston, Mass., 10th mo. 2d, 1837, third paragraph

reason: The sentence stands word for word in Letter XII of the Knapp edition, in the paragraph that begins with the anti-slavery cause as the high school of morals, with only italics on rights, moral and all that plain text drops. The Quaker date 10th mo. 2d, 1837 is 2 October 1837, and Grimké is unshipped, unbanned and at zero for the year.
